18:3857-1986 

Indian Standard 

METHOD FOR 

DETERMINATION OF COLOUR FASTNESS OF 

TEXTILE MATERIALS TO ACIP- FELTING : MILD 

( First Revision ) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on IS October 1986, after the draft finalized by the 
Chemical Methods of Test Sectional Committee had been approved by 
the Textile Division Council. 

0.2 This standard was first published in 1966 and has been revised to 
align it with ISO lOS-E 14-1978 'Textiles -r- Test for colour fastness to 
add-fetting : Mild\ issued by the Internatiotial Organization for Stan- 
dai^dization ( ISO )• Changes have been made for preparation, of test 
specimens, composite specimen, and for sampling. It differs from ISO 
standard in respect of sampling of the textile materials. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes a method for determination of colour fast- 
ness of textile materials of all kinds and in all forms to the ^^tion of 
dilute hot mineral acids, as used in mild felting conditions in^thehat'* 
making and felt industries. 

2. PRINCIFLE .^ 

2*1 A specimen o? the textile in contact with adjacent fabrics is milled 
in acid solution, rinsed and dried. The change in colour of the specimen 
and the tuMng of the adjacent fabrics is assessed with the standai^d grey 
scales. 

3« 8AMPUN6 

3.1 SamiriletodetermiM cmformity of a lot to this specification shall 
be tetocttd so ti to be te^wtttati ve of the lot 



15:3857-1986 

3.2 Sample drawn in compliance with the material spccirication or as 
agreed to between the buyer and the seller to evaluate the colour fastness 
of the textile material in the lot to acid — felting : mild, shall be held to 
be representative of the lot. 

4. APPARATUS 

4.1 A suitable receptacle and a glass rod flattened at one end» or an 
appropriate mechanical device ( sec Note )* 

Note — - Launderonietcr, of American Association of Textile Chemists and 
Colourists or Washwhecl-sponsored by the Society of J>ycrs and Colourlsts, may 
be used. Other mechanical devices may also be used for the tests provided that 
the results are identical to those obtained with the apparatus described in 4.1. 

4.2 Two adjacent fabrics, each measuring 10 x 4 cm, one piece made of 
wool and the other also made of wool or of another fibre to be assessed 
for staining, as desired ( see Appendix A ). 

4.3 Grey scales for assessing change in colour and staining (see 
IS : 768-1982* and IS : 769-1982t ). 

5. REAGENTS 

5.0 Quality of Reagents — Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals 
shall be employed in tests and distilled water ( see IS : 1070- 1977| ) shall 
be used where the use of water as reagent is intended. 

Jin 

NoTB — *Pure chemicals* shall mean chemicals that do not contain Impurities 
which affect the experimental results. 

5tl Salphnric Acid Solution — Containing 1 ml of concentrated sulphuric 
acid ( sp gr 1*84 ) per litre. 

6. PREPARATION OF TEST SPECIMENS AND COMPOSITE 
SPECIMEN 

6.1 If the textile to be tested is fabric, draw at least three test speci** 
mens 10 x 4 cm from the test sample ( see 3.2 ). Place a test specimen 
between two adjacent fabrics ( see 4.2 ) and sew along all four sides to 
form a composite specimen. Similarly, treat other tost specimens to form 
composite specimens. 

6.2 If the textile to be tested is yarn, knit or weave the test samide 
( see $.2 ) into a fabric and treat as in 6.1, or form a layer of parallel 

•Metiiod for evaluating change in cdour I first re^lsUm ). 

tMethod for evaluating staining {fint fefishn ). 

tSpecttcation for water for geoeral laboratof} use ( setenJreHsUm ). 



IS:38S7-19M 

lengths of yarn between the two adjacent fabrics ( see 4.2 ), the amount 
of yarn taken being approximately equal to half the combined mass 
of the adjacent fabrics. Sew along all four sides to hold the yarn in 
place and to form a composite specimen. Prepare at least three such 
composite specimens. 

6.3 If the textile to be tested is loose fibre ( see 3.2 ), comb and com* 
press an amount, from the test sample, approximately equal to half the 
combined mass of the adjacent fabrics {see 4.2 ) into a sheet 10 X 4 cm. 
Place the sheet between the two adjacent fabrics, and sew along all four 
sides to hold the fibres in place and to form a composite specimen. 
Prepare at least three such composite specimens. 

7. PROCEDURE 

7.1 Take the requisiteamount of sulphuric acid in a container to give 
a liquor to material ratio of 40 : 1. Raise the temperature of the solution 
to 60 ± 2''C. Immerse the composite specimen in the situation and mill 
it for 1 hour at 60 ± 2X ( see Notes 1 and 2 ). 

Note 1 — A mechanical milling device set which gives results, identical with 
those of band milling, may be used. 

Note 2 — During milling by hand, move the composite specimen continuously 
with the glass rod while it is in the milling bath and press it with the rod every 
two minutes, without removing from the bath. 

7.2 Remove the composite specimen, rinse it for 10 minutes in cold 
running water and drain it. Remove the stitching along all sides except 
one of the shorter sides. Open out the composite specimen wddryit 
by hanging in air at a temperature not exceeding 6QI^C with the three 
parts in contact only along the remaining line of stitching. j 

7.3 Evaluate the change in colour of the treated test specimens by the 
method prescribed in IS : 768-1982* and the degree of staintog of the 
two adjacent fabrics by the method prescribed in IS : 769-l982t ( see 
Notes 1 antf^2 ). 

Note 1 — Treated test specimens and the two adjacent fabrics should be 
allowed to cool after drying to regain their normal moisture content before 
evaluation. ^^ 

Nora 2 •* In cAses of doubt in th^ colour fastness rating at assessed by an ob« 

server, the assessment may be made by three otnervers and the overall average 
rating may be reported accordingly. 

7.4 Repeat the test with the remaining composite specimens.

tMetlod for evaluating staining (>!i*ji revision ).

of the test specimens and (b) the numerical ratings for stainings of the 
two adjacent Aibrks used in the preparation of the composite specii^ens.

AMENDMENT NO. 1 SEPTEMBER 2003 

TO 

IS 3857 : 1986 METHOD FOR DETERMINATION OF 

COLOUR FASTNESS OF TEXTILE MATERULS 

TO ACID — FELTING : MILD 

( First Revision ) 

(This amendment is being issued to make provision for use of multifibre 
adjacent fabric also.) 

( Page 3, clause 2.1 ) — Substitute 'adjacent fabric{s)'/<''' 'adjacent fabrics* 
wherever appearing. 

( Page 4, clause A.2 ) — Substitute the following for the existing clause: 

*4.2 Two single fibre adjacent fabrics, each measuring 10 cm x 4 cm, one piece 
made of wool and other also made of wool or of another fibre to be assessed for 
staining as desired (see also Appendix A).* 

( Page 4, clause 4.3 ) — Insert the following new clause after 4.3: 

'4.4 Multifibre Adjacent Fabrk — Measuring 10 cm x 4 cm.* 

( Page 4, clause 6.1 ) — Insert \see Notes after 6 J)' at the end. 

( Page S, clause 6.2 ) — Insert \see Notes after 6 J)' at the end. 

( Page 5, clause 6.3 ) — Insert \see Notes below)' at the end. 

( Page S, clause 63 ) — Insert the following Notes at the end of clause: 

•NOTES 

1 Klultifibre adjacent fabric may also be used in place of single fibre adjacent fabrics in 
which case the adjacent fabric shall cover only the face side of the test specimen 
(see IS 1025 1 : 1982 General principles of testing textiles for colour fastness). 

2 If the specimen is fabric, it is placed with its face in contact with the multifibre fabric 
and sewen along one short side. 



Amend No. 1 to IS 3857 : 1986 

3 If tM specimen U yarn or lo6se fibres an amoOnl approximtfely equal to mass of the 
multifibre adjacent fabric is evenly spread over the multifibre adjacent fabric, yam being 
iai4 at right angles to the individual stripe This is then covered with an equal size piece 
of light weight, non-stalnmg quality of polypropylene fabric, stitched along all four sides 
and in addition between e^ch pair of adjacent stripes compristog the multifibfie adjacent 
fabric/ 

( Page 5, clause 73, Note 1 ) — Substitute the following for the existing: 

'NOTE 1 — Treated test specimen and the adjacent fabric (single fibre or multifibre as 
the case may be) should be allowed to cool after drying to regain their f^prmal moisture 
content before evaluation ' 

( Page 6, clause 8.1, line 3 ) — Substitute 'adjacent fabric(5)' yfar 'adjacent 
fabrics*.
